approved_body:
Dear {{instructor_name}},

Your MorphoCloud course "{{course_name}}" has been approved.

Step 1 — Accept your GitHub invitation(s)
Before you can access your course repository ({{repo_name}}), accept your pending GitHub invitation(s):

  • The MorphoCloud organization invitation.
  • The {{repo_name}} repository invitation (or the link GitHub emailed you).

What happens next
We're finishing the setup of your course environment (compute allocation and the course runner). You'll receive a second email — "Your course is ready" — once it's provisioned, with your student roster and how to enroll students and launch instances. Please wait for that email before creating any instances.

Questions? Contact {{contact_email}}

— The MorphoCloud Team

student_invited_subject: You're enrolled in {{course_name}} on MorphoCloud - accept your invitation
student_invited_body:
Hi,

You've been enrolled in the MorphoCloud course "{{course_name}}".

Action required — accept your GitHub invitation (it expires in 7 days):

  1. Go to your GitHub organizations page.
  2. Accept the pending invitation from MorphoCloud.

Once you've accepted, request your cloud instance:

  1. Open your course repository.
  2. Open a new Course Instance Request issue and follow the prompts.
  3. Post /create as a comment to launch your instance. You'll get an email with your connection details when it's ready.

Questions? Contact your instructor or {{contact_email}}.

— The MorphoCloud Team

course_ready_body:
Dear {{instructor_name}},

Your MorphoCloud course "{{course_name}}" is ready. (If you haven't accepted your own GitHub invitation yet, do that here.)

Enrolling each student has TWO parts — you must do BOTH:

  1. Add them to your roster (Google Sheet) — supplies their email.
  2. Add them to roster-handles.txt (course repo) — invites them to GitHub and gives them access.

Part 1 — Your course roster (Google Sheet, {{roster_shared}})
{{roster_url}}

  • Column A is github_handle, Column B is email. Do not rename, move, or delete the header row — the system looks these columns up by name, and changing them will stop instance emails from reaching your students.
  • Add your own GitHub handle and email as the first entry (row 2, directly under the header) so you can test /create right away and receive instance emails yourself.

The roster only supplies emails; it does not grant access — that's Part 2.

Part 2 — Enroll everyone who will be using the course repo (GitHub)
Paste the github_handle values (one per line) into roster-handles.txt in your course repository, then commit and push:
{{repo_url}}

This is what invites people — include students, TAs, co-instructors, and anyone else who will work in the course repo. Each person is sent a GitHub invitation they must accept within 7 days (it expires after that); until they accept, they have no access and can't create an instance.

⚠ If you skip Part 2, your students are never invited and never get access. Enrollment is ongoing, not one-time — you can add people at any point, as long as you add each one to both the roster (Google Sheet) and roster-handles.txt (GitHub repo).

Launching instances
After accepting their invitation, a student opens an Course Instance Request issue and posts /create. They get an email with connection details when the instance is ready.

Courses with more than 9 participants
JetStream2 enforces a default per-allocation quota of 25 instances and 10 volumes. If your total headcount (students + instructors) exceeds 9, request a quota increase before the course starts — to headcount + 2, for both instances and volumes — via an ACCESS support ticket. Details and boilerplate.

A note about emails
The emails that matter come from no-reply@morphocloud.org (credentials, enrollment, action items) — remind students to check spam. GitHub's own notifications can be ignored.

Documentation: Post-approval setup guide · Instructor overview

Questions? Contact {{contact_email}}

— The MorphoCloud Team
